title: Helios Console — Access
description: Role-capability configuration for the Helios Console macOS app. Preference domain MUST be com.herojoneslabs.helios.console.access — deploy as its own Jamf Pro Application & Custom Settings profile. NOTHING IS HARDCODED IN THE APP: every capability a user has — which sidebar modules render, which device actions they may run, which cleanup sub-actions they may run, whether they may export data out of the app — is defined by the `roles` block below. Roles are ARBITRARY, ADMIN-NAMED capability sets; the app ships no built-in role names, no built-in tiers, and no built-in capability defaults. IDENTITY: when the core domain sets signIn.method=entra, the signed-in user's role names come from the Entra token's roles claim; otherwise the machine-scoped `role` key below names a single role. A user matching several roles receives the UNION of their capabilities. FAIL-CLOSED GUARANTEE: no `roles` block — or a role name matching no entry's `name` field — grants NOTHING; a Mac that never receives this profile runs Helios as an EMPTY app (no modules, no actions), so under-scoping is safe, over-scoping is not. SCOPING CHANGED IN 2.4: because the `roles` block now carries every capability, it must reach every Mac whose users need one — scope this profile (with the `role`/`deviceActions` appropriate to each population) to ALL Macs running Helios, not admin Macs only. PAIRED SCOPING: any variant whose roles grant destructive computerActions (e.g. wipe, returnToService) must be scoped to the same Macs as any write-capable variant of the com.herojoneslabs.helios.console.credentials profile (see docs/ConfigProfileMigration.md). SECURITY: managed-preference plists are world-readable on disk — every value delivered here is visible to any local user of the Mac.

configurationVersion.title: Configuration Version
configurationVersion.description: Schema/profile version stamp (informational — the app logs it, nothing else reads it).

role.title: Role Name (MDM sign-in mode only)
role.description: FREE-FORM role name, consulted ONLY when Entra sign-in is NOT configured (the core domain's signIn block is absent, or signIn.method=email). The value must EXACTLY match the `name` field of an entry in the `roles` list below — matching is case-sensitive and literal; there is no fuzzy match and no aliasing. When signIn.method=entra this key is IGNORED ENTIRELY: role names then come from the Entra token's roles claim. Deliberately NO default and NO enum — the app knows no role names, so nothing can be assumed. Absent, blank, or unmatched → the user still signs in but sees an EMPTY app: no modules, no device actions, no cleanup, no export (fail-closed; a missing or broken profile must not hard-lock an org out of the app entirely). MDM mode resolves exactly ONE role — union semantics apply only to Entra mode, where a token can carry several role values. Deliver one profile variant per Mac population (e.g. role=Helios.Support on support Macs, role=Helios.Admin on admin Macs).

roles.title: Role Definitions (capability sets)
roles.description: THE capability source of truth — a LIST of arbitrary, ADMIN-NAMED capability sets. Each entry carries its role name in the `name` field (e.g. Helios.Admin, Helios.Support, HelpDesk.Tier1); the app ships no built-in names and no defaults, so whatever you define here is exactly what exists. NAME MATCHING IS EXACT AND CASE-SENSITIVE: in Entra sign-in mode a `name` must equal an app-role VALUE on the sign-in app registration character-for-character; in MDM mode it must equal the `role` key above. MULTI-ROLE = UNION: a user matching several entries receives the union of every matched role's lists, and allowExport is OR'd across them. A cleanup-only role (modules = [cleanup]) is a supported pattern — assign it alongside another role and the union applies. FAIL-CLOSED: an absent `roles` block, or a role name matching no entry, grants NOTHING — in Entra mode such a user is REFUSED sign-in; in MDM mode the user signs in to an empty app. There is deliberately NO default for this block: a default would be a hardcoded capability, which is precisely what this model removes. Unknown ids inside a role's lists are IGNORED (logged once) so newer profiles deploy safely to older app builds. EDGE CASES: an entry with a missing or blank `name` is SKIPPED (it is unreachable — no role name could match it); two entries sharing a `name` are UNIONED (later entries add to, never replace, earlier ones), so a duplicate can only ever widen that name's grants. JAMF EDITOR NOTE: this block is a LIST OF OBJECTS precisely so Jamf Pro's Application & Custom Settings form generator can render it — a dictionary keyed by admin-chosen role names could only be expressed as `additionalProperties`, which that editor cannot render, forcing raw XML editing. Same idiom as deviceActions.computer.actions below. See Deployment/sample.mobileconfig for a working example.

items.title: Role Definition
items.description: The complete capability set granted by one role name. Every list is additive within a role and unioned across a user's matched roles. Omitted list = that role grants nothing of that kind.

name.title: Role Name
name.description: Admin-chosen role name — REQUIRED; an entry without one is skipped as unreachable. Must match an Entra app-role Value (Entra sign-in mode) or the `role` key above (MDM mode), exactly and case-sensitively. Reusing a name across entries unions their capabilities rather than replacing them.

modules.title: Modules (sidebar / route ids)
modules.description: Sidebar/route ids this role may see and open. ROLE-DRIVEN ONLY — there is no machine-scoped second layer for modules. Absent or empty = no modules at all. Omitting `settings` does NOT strand the user: Sign Out lives in the sidebar, not inside Settings. The `cleanup` module is no longer special-cased — it is simply the `cleanup` id in this list (pair it with cleanupActions below, which is what makes the module useful). `myDevice` is RESERVED for a per-user single-device view shipping in a FOLLOW-UP PR: it is accepted here today but INERT (unimplemented ids are ignored), so you may pre-stage it safely. Presentation of the sidebar — order, labels, icons — is configured separately in the ui domain's sidebarItems; this list controls whether the role may access an id at all.

computerActions.title: Allowed Computer Actions — usable by THIS ROLE (layer 2 of 2)
computerActions.description: Computer DeviceAction ids this role may USE. TWO LAYERS, BOTH MUST ALLOW: deviceActions.computer.actions below decides which actions EXIST on this Mac (enabled state, menu label, Return-to-Service options); THIS list decides which of those the role may see and run. Only the intersection renders and executes — an id listed here that the machine allow-list does not grant (or grants with enabled=false) stays hidden AND blocked, and an id the allow-list grants that no matched role lists stays hidden AND blocked. Absent or empty = no computer actions for this role. Reserved ids (lock, viewRecoveryLockPassword, updateInventory, renewMDMProfile, sendCustomCommand, installPackage, runPolicy) render nothing regardless of either layer.

mobileDeviceActions.title: Allowed Mobile Device Actions — usable by THIS ROLE (layer 2 of 2)
mobileDeviceActions.description: Mobile-device DeviceAction ids this role may USE. Same two-layer rule as computerActions: deviceActions.mobileDevice.actions decides existence, this list decides role access, and only the intersection renders. Forward-looking — the mobile device detail view has no actions menu yet, so nothing renders from this list today. Absent or empty = none.

cleanupActions.title: Allowed Cleanup Sub-Actions (for this role)
cleanupActions.description: Cleanup sub-actions this role may run. ROLE-DRIVEN ONLY — there is no machine-scoped allow-list for cleanup sub-actions (unlike device actions). Absent or empty = none, even when the role's modules include `cleanup`: the module then renders with nothing runnable in it. Grant `cleanup` in modules AND the sub-actions here to make the module useful. deleteFromProtect requires the core domain's jamfProtect block to be configured; deleteRecord and unmanage are destructive — pair them with write-capable credentials scoping.

allowExport.title: Allow Export / Download
allowExport.description: Whether this role may extract data out of the app. Gates EVERY export surface, not Reports alone: the Reports export menu (CSV / Excel / PDF / Markdown), BOTH Cleanup export menus (the stale-device and protected-device lists), and the Logs module's Export CSV button (which copies the whole audit trail to the pasteboard). Without this flag those controls do not render at all. OR'd across a user's matched roles — one role granting it is enough. Absent = false (fail-closed). Only meaningful alongside the modules that host those surfaces (`reports`, `cleanup`, `logs`): e.g. a role granting `cleanup` but omitting allowExport gets the Cleanup module with no export control.

cleanup.title: Cleanup (Stale Device) Settings
cleanup.description: TUNABLES ONLY for the Cleanup module — this block grants NOTHING. Visibility of the module comes from `cleanup` in a role's modules list, and which sub-actions run comes from that role's cleanupActions list. staleDays is the DEFAULT stale threshold; users can change it in-app unless you re-deliver this profile to reset it.

staleDays.title: Stale Threshold (days)
staleDays.description: Days without check-in before a device counts as stale. Deliver as an integer; the app also tolerates a string value (e.g. "90") because some deployed profiles ship it that way.

defaultStaticGroupID.title: Default Static Group ID
defaultStaticGroupID.description: Jamf static group ID pre-selected for Cleanup runs. Delivered as a string; parsed to an integer downstream.

defaultSiteID.title: Default Site ID
defaultSiteID.description: Jamf site ID pre-selected for Cleanup runs. Delivered as a string; parsed to an integer downstream.

deviceActions.title: Device Actions — available on THIS MAC (layer 1 of 2; layer 2 is each role's Allowed Actions, under Role Definitions)
deviceActions.description: STRICT FAIL-CLOSED per-action allow-list for the device Actions menu. LAYER 1 OF 2: this block decides which actions EXIST on THIS Mac (enabled state, menu label, Return-to-Service options); a `roles` entry's computerActions / mobileDeviceActions decide which of those a given USER may see and run. An action renders and executes only when BOTH layers allow it — neither layer can expand what the other denies. If no actions array is delivered for a platform, that platform's Actions menu is HIDDEN ENTIRELY. If the array is present, ONLY listed actions with enabled=true are shown (and executable) — an id not listed, or listed with enabled=false, is hidden AND blocked at execution. Unknown ids are ignored (logged once) so newer profiles deploy safely to older app builds. The computer id "wipe" is now IMPLEMENTED — a bare erase (ERASE_DEVICE with recovery PIN) that ALWAYS waits for the device to acknowledge and keeps the Jamf record and Entra object; lock, viewRecoveryLockPassword, updateInventory, renewMDMProfile, sendCustomCommand, installPackage, and runPolicy remain reserved — granting them renders nothing. displayName overrides the menu label only. LEGACY: the app still decodes the pre-2.1 boolean-map shape (e.g. computer.restart=true) when no actions array is delivered — explicitly delivered keys become grants, and the old per-key defaults are no longer applied — but this schema (2.1+) exposes ONLY the actions array; computer/mobileDevice reject any other property, so profiles built or edited from this schema cannot reintroduce the old flat keys. Migrate deployed legacy profiles to the actions array. The core domain's jamfPro.screenShareEnabled key is DEPRECATED: once an allow-list is delivered it is authoritative for screenShare too.

displayName.title: Menu Label Override
displayName.description: Overrides the Actions-menu label ONLY. Confirmation-dialog safety copy is app-built-in and never profile-controlled. Empty = built-in label.

options.title: Action Options (Return to Service)
options.description: Consulted ONLY by the returnToService action; ignored for every other id. Both toggles default true, so omitting this object keeps the original full-decommission behavior. The erase always runs first and ALWAYS waits for the device to acknowledge ERASE_DEVICE — no cleanup step runs without that acknowledgment. deleteEntraObject auto-skips when Entra isn't configured.

deleteJamfRecord.title: Delete Jamf Pro Record
deleteJamfRecord.description: Remove the computer record from Jamf Pro after the erase is acknowledged.

deleteEntraObject.title: Delete Entra Device Object
deleteEntraObject.description: Delete the device object from Microsoft Entra after the erase is acknowledged, so the device can re-enroll cleanly.

mobileDevice.title: Mobile Device Actions
mobileDevice.description: Forward-looking: the mobile device detail view has no actions menu yet. Any future menu is built from this allow-list from day one.

displayName.title: Menu Label Override
displayName.description: Overrides the Actions-menu label ONLY. Confirmation-dialog safety copy is app-built-in and never profile-controlled. Empty = built-in label.
